title: Knowledge check: How Express Connects to Databases

questions.prompt: In How Express Connects to Databases, which statement best describes Express versus a database driver?
options: Express does not supply a database driver. Use an established driver or ORM, parameterize data values, preserve database constraints, manage connections and test rollback/error cases.
This option describes a different concept and does not define express versus a database driver (choice 2).
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
questions.answer_key: Express does not supply a database driver. Use an established driver or ORM, parameterize data values, preserve database constraints, manage connections and test rollback/error cases.
questions.explanation: Express does not supply a database driver. Use an established driver or ORM, parameterize data values, preserve database constraints, manage connections and test rollback/error cases.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying How Express Connects to Databases?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Express does not include a database driver. Keep route matching, business services, and persistence separate; parameterize values, respect database constraints and transactions, and manage pooling and timeouts.
questions.answer_key: Express does not include a database driver. Keep route matching, business services, and persistence separate; parameterize values, respect database constraints and transactions, and manage pooling and timeouts.
questions.explanation: Express does not include a database driver. Keep route matching, business services, and persistence separate; parameterize values, respect database constraints and transactions, and manage pooling and timeouts.

questions.prompt: A change related to How Express Connects to Databases appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
